c74object.name: zerr.envelopes~
c74object.digest: Generate one envelope per speaker from a control signal, by trajectory or by trigger
c74object.description: Use the zerr.envelopes~ object to turn a control signal and a speaker layout into a multi-channel set of envelopes, one per loudspeaker. In trajectory mode the control signal is a position along a chain of speakers and the envelopes crossfade between neighbours. In trigger mode every pulse makes the sound jump to a speaker connected to the current one. The output feeds zerr.disperser~ directly or through zerr.combinator~.

inlet.description: In trajectory mode a position from 0 to 1 along the trajectory chain. In trigger mode a pulse train: every time the signal reaches 1 the sound jumps. The pulse must touch 1.0 exactly (a peak at 0.99 never fires), and a signal held at 1 keeps jumping sample by sample, so send pulses and use interval to cap the rate. All messages go here.
How far a jump spills onto the neighbouring speakers, from 0 (one speaker) to 1 (widest). Ignored in trajectory mode.
Multiplies every envelope. Reads 1 when nothing is connected, so a plain object plays at full level.

outlet.description: A multi-channel signal with one channel per loudspeaker, in the layout file's numbering. Connect it to the right inlet of zerr.disperser~ or to an inlet of zerr.combinator~.

objarg.name: mode
objarg.description: trajectory (default): the control signal pans along a chain of speakers. trigger: each pulse jumps to a connected speaker.

objarg.name: layout
objarg.digest: Speaker layout YAML on the search path
objarg.description: The name of a layout YAML file, with or without the extension. The package ships quad_4, ring_8, line_16 and ambisonic_21 in its misc folder; your own file anywhere on the search path works too. Without this argument the object uses a built-in ring of eight speakers, the same positions as ring_8.

method.name: signal
method.description: See the inlet descriptions. All three inlets are signals.

method.name: active
method.description: active set replaces the active set, active add and active del change it. Speaker numbers are the ones in the layout file. Only active speakers may appear in traj, topo and curr: a traj or topo set with an inactive number is refused, topo add and topo del skip it. active set replaces the list and resets the trajectory (numeric order) and the topology (fully connected); an unknown speaker number refuses the whole message. active add only activates; the new speaker joins no trajectory or topology until you put it there. active del removes the speakers from the active list, the trajectory and every topology row, and is refused if it would leave no active speaker or an empty trajectory; if the current speaker goes, the sound moves to the first one still active. A speaker with no links left keeps the trigger on itself.

method.name: traj
method.digest: The chain trajectory mode pans along
method.description: The ordered list of speakers the control signal travels through in trajectory mode: 0 is the first speaker in the list, 1 the last.

method.name: topo
method.digest: Which speakers a trigger may jump to
method.description: Defines the connections used in trigger mode: the first number is the speaker you jump from, the rest are the speakers a jump may land on. topo set replaces that speaker's list, topo add and topo del change it. One message per source speaker; separate several with commas.

method.name: curr
method.description: Moves the sound to that speaker without waiting for a pulse.

method.name: interval
method.digest: Minimum time between two jumps (trigger mode)
method.description: Pulses arriving sooner than this after a jump are ignored.

method.name: print
method.description: Posts the active speakers, the trajectory and the topology to the Max Console.

method.name: bang
method.description: Posts the package version, the mode, the layout, the channel count, the signal vector size and the sample rate to the Max Console.

c74object.discussion: A layout file lists one position per speaker, in Cartesian (x, y, z) or spherical coordinates; the speaker numbering of the file is the channel order of the outlet. By default the trajectory runs through all active speakers in numeric order and every active speaker is connected to all of them, itself included, so a trigger may jump anywhere; reshape both at any time with traj and topo. In trigger mode the envelopes are power-normalised: raising the spread shares the energy over more speakers without raising the total, and the gain multiplies everything afterwards. The console posts the layout path at creation and bang posts the configuration, so you can check which layout loaded. Several zerr.envelopes~ objects driven by different features can be merged with zerr.combinator~ before zerr.disperser~.

entry.name: multi-channel signal
entry.description: One envelope per loudspeaker, in layout order.
